name: Sociology
notice: Study material, not professional advice. SocGradify explains sociological theories, evidence and debates. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and haven't yet been reviewed by subject experts, so they may contain errors. Lessons separate empirical findings from theoretical interpretations and from normative arguments, and statistics carry their source and year: check the latest release before relying on a figure.

paths.name: A level Sociology
paths.sub: The core of A level and equivalent courses: theory, culture and identity, families, education, crime, beliefs and methods.

paths.name: University year 1
paths.sub: The first-year core of a sociology degree: the discipline, classical and contemporary theory, inequality and methods.

paths.name: Social theory
paths.sub: From Comte, Marx, Durkheim and Weber to feminism, Foucault, Bourdieu, Giddens and Beck.

paths.name: Inequality and social justice
paths.sub: Class, poverty, gender, race and migration, and how they shape education, health and life chances.

paths.name: Research skills
paths.sub: Research design, interviews, ethnography, content and discourse analysis, official data, reflexivity, statistics and reporting.

paths.name: Society and policy
paths.sub: The state, power, welfare, crime, health and the economy: sociology for policy and public life.

paths.name: Global and urban
paths.sub: Globalisation, cities, population, migration and the environment.
